Header:
Date: 2026-11-26
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes

Summary:
Zenith Edge is evaluating options to move away from their current hosted provider and to either adopt Redwood Hosted for immediate lift-and-shift, reserve Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, or run Redwood Private in their VPC for data residency. Primary concerns: eval parity (TGI/vLLM), latency and cost tradeoffs, KV cache warmup, SOC2/SSO/KMS needs, and pilot timeline. They requested benchmark artifacts and a private deploy demo.

Topics:
- current stack: Anthropic + some vLLM on prem for high-throughput inference
- parity for instruction-following models and reranking
- private deployment network/egress constraints
- quantization and token-cost tradeoffs

Action items (as discussed): see action_items metadata above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. Im Maya from Redwood, AE on the west coast, i'll kick us off.
[00:05] Marco: yeah, thanks, um, quick note, we only have 50 minutes so we want to focus on the migration fit.
[00:12] Liam: hi, im Liam, head of ml, Priya's on infra, marco's the exec sponsor.
[00:17] Priya: hey, hi.
[00:19] Ethan: Ethan Ross, solutions engineer, i'll cover compatibility and benchmarks.
[00:23] Marco: quick background: we've been on Anthropic for convo, some endpoints on OpenAI and a small vLLM fleet for heavy throughput. We're exploring untethering from the hosted provider — reduce egress and vendor lock, plus better cost predictability.
[00:36] Maya: great. two immediate levers people choose: hosted to move fast, dedicated to lock capacity, private if you need VPC + KMS. Where are you leaning?
[00:45] Liam: leaning private for PII workloads, but want hosted for lighter traffic and burst. two questions: parity with vLLM/TGI workflows and how re-using our prompt/eval suites looks.
[00:58] Ethan: for vLLM/TGI parity, we map model artifacts and tokenizer behavior, usually compatibility is high but there are edge differences in sampling seeds and kv cache behavior. we provide a benchmark harness — you can run your eval set across hosted/dedicated/private with same model artifacts.
[01:20] Priya: when you say kv cache differences, can you explain? we've seen warmup spikes in inference.
[01:26] Ethan: yeah, so runtime-level kv handling varies: some vLLM builds keep a different chunking for long context which affects memory and first-token latency. Redwood's runtime has continuous batching and prefix cache to mitigate warmups, but per-model kernel selection matters. we'll show numbers.
[01:44] Liam: latency targets: p95 < 220ms for short prompts, cost target is about 40% below current per-token for the mid-tier Llama family. realistic?
[01:55] Maya: it's doable depending on batching and quantization. dedicated with q4_0-like quant can cut unit cost; hosted has optimizations too, but heavy bursty patterns favor dedicated.
[02:10] Marco: security — we need SOC2+ISO, SAML SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration for key management. can private support HSM?
[02:20] Ethan: yes, private supports KMS and can be configured to use customer-managed keys, HSM via partner integrations is possible, and audit logs are exposed through the console and can be shipped to your SIEM.
[02:33] Priya: egress constraints — we have strict whitelisting and no external storage. how does the private deploy handle model pulls and updates?
[02:40] Ethan: private has a controlled update path: optionally air-gapped package or controlled model sync using your internal registry. model pulls can be initiated from within your VPC; we don't require outbound connectivity for runtime after install.
[02:53] Liam: eval parity specifics: our eval harness uses TGI with sampling top-p=0.9, temperature 0.2, and custom rerank step using embeddings. does Redwood support embeddings and reranking in same pipeline?
[03:05] Ethan: yes, the API supports generation + embeddings + rerank chains, and you can pin model versions. small caveat: embedding model families differ, but we provide mapping and embedding parity tests.
[03:19] Marco: what's the effort to move our vLLM jobs to Redwood Dedicated? we have a dozen endpoints, each with 2k reqs/s at peak.
[03:27] Ethan: we size capacity by token throughput and concurrency. dedicated pools can be reserved with burst capacity; we usually run a short performance exercise to calibrate batch sizes and sequencing to reach your 2k RPS. typical pilot is 2-4 weeks of load tests.
[03:44] Priya: network: will we need to open many ports? we prefer a single egress/ingress endpoint behind our load balancer.
[03:51] Maya: private can be fronted by your LB; dedicated and hosted use standard HTTPS endpoints. we'll provide network diagrams.
[03:59] Liam: about retraining/finetuning — we currently do light fine-tune on some models, can we bring fine-tuned weights?
[04:06] Ethan: yes, you can bring artifacts. we support model weight import and you can register them in the model catalog. for security we support encrypted storage and access controls.
[04:17] Marco: cost model question: if we run mixed hosting (hosted for spikes, dedicated for baseline), how do fallbacks work on capacity pressure?
[04:26] Maya: smart routing policy can route by latency or cost; during capacity constraint fallback can go to a cheaper model variant or a hosted fallback region. policies are configurable per-route.
[04:40] Priya: demo ask: can we see the private deploy jumpbox and the control plane? we want to validate how RBAC and audit logs appear.
[04:49] Maya: yes, we can schedule a demo environment. Ethan, i'll need to coordinate the infra session with Priya.
[04:54] Ethan: noted. i'll prep a quick runbook and show the model import path and the audit log exports.
[05:00] Liam: benchmarking — we'll run our eval suite: instruction-following + retrieval+rerank. what's the template?
[05:06] Ethan: we'll share a benchmark template (csv + scripts). it's important you include sequence length percentiles and your typical prompt mix; we'll correlate tokenization differences and sampling seeds.
[05:19] Marco: timeline: we want to pilot in jan, go live feb/mar if all good. risks?
[05:24] Maya: common risks are eval drift due to sampling differences, and network constraints for private. mitigations: pin seeds where possible, run paired evaluations side-by-side, and do a short warmup phase for kv caches.
[05:40] Priya: questions about SLA: what uptime and latency SLOs look like for dedicated?
[05:46] Maya: dedicated comes with a 99.9% uptime SLA and latency targets per model tier; we can include a latency credit mechanism in the contract.
[05:55] Liam: anything on compliance posture for EU data residency?
[06:00] Ethan: hosted supports region pinning; private obviously keeps data in your region/VPC. we can provide EU-hosted consoles and logs as needed.
[06:10] Marco: ok let's talk technical specifics — sample rate limiting and throttling behavior is critical for our scraping pipeline.
[06:17] Ethan: we support token and request quotas per API key and per-route throttles. for burst absorbing we recommend using dedicated pools with a small hosted fallback quota.
[06:29] Liam: any gotchas with tokenizer mismatches migrating from TGI? we've seen off-by-one in prompt offsets.
[06:36] Ethan: yeah, sometimes TGI's tokenizer segmentation differs; we do a tokenization parity pass in the benchmark and provide mapping utilities. also reproducibility across runtimes can vary; we'll surface diffs.
[06:49] Priya: ok, on private deployment — what's the install footprint? our nodes are AMD instances with 80GB GPU, is that supported?
[06:57] Ethan: supported hardware varies; we have profiles for common GPU types. if you're on AMD we validate kernels and will run a preflight. some optimizations are Intel/NVIDIA specific but we have fallback kernels.
[07:12] Maya: just to capture decisions: you want a hosted pilot for non-PII, private for PII, and a Dedicated contention plan?
[07:19] Marco: yes that is the tentative plan.
[07:22] Liam: ok, next step, send pricing + compatibility checklist; then we'll share eval artifacts.
[07:27] Maya: great, we'll do that.
[07:30] Priya: quick note — we need to include security team in the demo; i'll loop in Aisha (sec).
[07:36] Ethan: i'll include audit log export examples in the demo.
[07:40] Marco: thanks all.

Close / Recap:
[51:30] Maya: recap: Maya sends pricing and SLA, Ethan sends vLLM/TGI compatibility checklist and benchmark template, Priya to provide model endpoints and seq length percentiles. schedule private jumpbox demo first week of Dec.

[51:55] Maya: thanks everyone. bye.
